results.evidence: Three independent sources grade the route IV 5.10b: a 2007 CascadeClimbers trip report titled 'Gato Negro IV 5.10b', a 2009 Washington Pass modern-classics list ('Gato Negro IV 5.10b**'), and a 2013 blog trip report ('IV 5.10b'). The route's main database page calls it 5.10 with 'fairly sustained 5.10a/b climbing'. Only one 2010 blog post gives 5.10d (and IV+); the FA note says 5.10+. 5.10b agrees with beta, pitch_detail and the waypoint note.

results.evidence: Sources split evenly. The FA report (AAC) and a 2010 trip report both say 11 pitches (the latter calls the splitter cracks 'the final 11th pitch'). The main route database lists 12 pitches, and a 2013 trip report names money pitches 8-11 and then 'skipped the final pitch', implying 12. No patch until a topo settles it.

results.evidence: Silver Star Mountain and the SR-20 pullout ~4 mi east of Washington Pass are in Okanogan County (Wikipedia: 'Silver Star Mountain (Okanogan County, Washington)'; topozone lists it in Okanogan County). The managing unit is the Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Methow Valley Ranger District (WTA and Mountaineers route pages). The county sheriff's contact page lists the non-emergency dispatch line 509-422-7232, and Okanogan County SAR's contact page lists the same number as Sheriff's Dispatch.

results.evidence: emergency.nearestHospital says Skagit Valley Hospital, Mount Vernon 'about 60 miles'. The pullout is on the Okanogan side of Washington Pass, and Mount Vernon is well over 100 road miles west on SR-20, so both the distance and possibly the choice of hospital (east-side Methow/Okanogan hospitals may be nearer) look wrong. Not researched to two sources in this pass; no patch.

The row carries a single 60 m rope in the rack while RAPPELS and BAILOUT call for double ropes. The main route page gives no rope or rappel detail. A 2010 report describes several raps over the top into a loose gully without stating rope count, and a 2013 report mentions teams sharing ropes but not the rap system. No two sources state the rope needed.

Sources themselves disagree: the FA report (AAC) places Gato Negro on 'the west face of Silver Star Mountain' on Whine Spire, south of the Wine Spires, while a 2010 trip report and the main route database call Whine Spire a sub-peak on Silver Star's East face. The descent runs in the gully between Whine Spire and Silver Star's west summit. The actual aspect of the climbed face could not be established from two agreeing sources.

No published elevation for Whine Spire was found; sources give only Silver Star's summits (east 8,876 ft, west just over 8,840 ft) and describe Whine Spire as lower than the west summit. Neither 7,800 nor 8,348 could be confirmed.

best_season contradicts itself (recommends late June, then says avoid June). The FA was made on June 21, 2001, and dated ascents found are late July and September; a snow patch at the start is noted by the route page. No two sources state a recommended window, so the prose was not rewritten.

A 2013 trip report calls it '1500 ft Gato Negro', while the route page and a 2010 report say most pitches are 180-190 ft and none under 150 ft over 11-12 pitches, which is ~1,800-2,200 ft of rope length. 1,500 ft may be face height rather than climbing distance, but no source states which; only one source gives a length.

A forum thread reports the small spring ~10 minutes north of the bench running plenty in mid-September and calling it very reliable. But a route summary says water at the bench and the col lasts only 'until late summer', and a June 2025 report found the stream near 6,400 ft dry. The sources disagree, so what_to_bring was left as is (bivy is out of scope).
